name: Squirtle
visual: Blue turtle, brown shell and curled tail.
note: Strong fit: horizontal paddling pose, with the curled tail kept visible.

name: Crush
visual: Green sea turtle with patterned shell and relaxed expression.
note: Strong fit: broad flippers and slow gliding give him a different movement style.

name: Hank
visual: Orange-red octopus with a large head and expressive eyes.
note: Strong fit: seven trailing arms and gentle jet-like swimming; needs an octopus animation.

name: Blooper
visual: Pink-and-white SNES squid with a pointed head, dark eye mask and short tentacles.
note: Original SNES sprite reference. Short pulses and trailing tentacles suit the tank.

name: Lapras
visual: Blue long-necked swimmer with a grey shell and four flippers.
note: A miniature interpretation; keep the head and shell readable while it glides.

name: Ariel
visual: Red hair, purple top and green mermaid tail.
note: Very recognizable colours; needs a horizontal swim pose and space for hair and tail.

name: Perry the Platypus
visual: Teal body, orange bill and flat patterned tail.
note: Use a streamlined paddling pose. Agent P’s hat could improve recognition at small scale.

name: Ecco
visual: Sleek grey dolphin with a long snout and curved dorsal fin.
note: Natural swimmer; preserve the head’s star markings so it reads as Ecco rather than a generic dolphin.

name: Squirt
visual: Small sea turtle with an oversized head and patterned shell.
note: A compact alternative to Crush, with quicker flipper beats.

name: Bailey
visual: White beluga with a rounded forehead and friendly face.
note: A tank-sized interpretation; pale colours and rounded profile would stand out.

name: Luca Paguro
visual: Blue-green sea-monster form with fins and a long tail.
note: Use the underwater form. Tail-driven swimming works, but limbs and face need more sprite space.

name: Starmie
visual: Purple star shape with a gold ring and red central gem.
note: A very different silhouette; gentle spinning suits it better than a fish’s tail wag.

name: Skipper
visual: Black-and-white penguin with an orange bill and determined eyebrows.
note: Use a horizontal diving pose and flipper strokes; eyebrows distinguish him from a generic penguin.

name: SpongeBob
visual: Yellow square sponge, brown shorts and red tie.
note: Comedic option: a horizontal paddling pose. Angular silhouette will be conspicuous among the fish.

name: Patrick Star
visual: Pink starfish wearing green shorts with purple flowers.
note: Comedic option: broad arm strokes and a slow glide; shorts carry much of the identity.

name: Squidward
visual: Pale turquoise head, long nose and brown shirt.
note: More of an adaptation: tentacles trailing behind in a swimming pose; long nose must remain readable.
